headline: EMBERWOOD — our own HD-2D Zelda-like is live
lede: Issue #738 asked for a fancier Zelda-like that is ours — genre and mechanics, never Nintendo's names or art. EMBERWOOD shipped to production as squash 6bfca16: hero Ash, the vale of Emberwood, embers for money, two item-gated dungeons and two bosses, all rendered as pixel sprites on a lit three.js diorama (real sun, torch point-lights, shadows, water, bloom, tilt-shift). Tap to play at /retrogames/emberwood.

notes.text: One overworld + a shop (potion/arrows/bombs/shield), six monster species each with its own AI, two dungeons with keys, locked + big doors, a push-block plate, cracked walls, far arrow-switches gated on the bow from dungeon 1, hearts and containers, death-and-respawn with progress kept.

A deterministic seeded solver proves both dungeons finishable with only the items owned at that point; a 61-gate harness (emberwoodcheck) audits maps, species, gating, slack, determinism and a real Chrome drive with zero page errors — and is mutation-proven to fail.

three.js r155+ lights use candela and the stage is +Z-up: the first HD-2D build rendered fully black until lights went to 4-7 candela, ACES tone-mapping was on, and the Y-up mental model was replaced with a Z-up stage. Screenshot the diorama and check a pixel histogram — a blank-check alone passes on a mis-framed all-black scene.

jalfern.com's proxy still serves a cached main bundle without the EMBERWOOD label string (same host-index staleness as #696/#694); the merge, Vercel SUCCESS and the production alias at 6bfca16 are all confirmed, so the title is live once the host index refreshes.
